claim.pdf_says: 'When the UNSTRING statement is initiated, the current receiving area is the data item referenced by identifier-4. Data is transferred from the data item referenced by identifier-1 to the data item referenced by identifier-4 according to the following rules:' ... 'Size is defined as number of character positions.' - all in plain roman type; no bold anywhere on the page.
claim.markdown_says: '... the current receiving area is the data item referenced by identifier-**4**. Data is transferred from the data item referenced by identifier-**1** to the data item referenced by identifier-**4** according to the following rules:' ... 'Size is defined as number of character positions**.**' - and likewise identifier-**7**, literal-**1**, identifier-**2**, identifier-**5**, identifier-**6** throughout general rule 11 a)-g).
claim.why_it_matters: Spurious markdown emphasis markers were injected around the trailing digit of every operand name (and around one full stop) on this page only. Nothing in the PDF is bold. The literal file text now reads 'identifier-**4**', so a grep, anchor scan or spec-citation tool searching for 'identifier-4' misses every occurrence in UNSTRING general rule 11 - the rule that defines the whole transfer algorithm.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, then corrected on two secondary details.

PDF side (E:/Temp/specrecon/v801/spec_p801.png, rendered at 300 dpi, 2550x3300): the entire body of page 801 is set in a single uniform roman weight. I cropped and enlarged the two passages the claim names. In the general rule 11 lead-in ('...referenced by identifier-4.  Data is transferred from the data item referenced by identifier-1 to the data item referenced by identifier-4 according to the following rules:') the digits '4' and '1' have stroke weights identical to the adjacent letters - no thickening, no wider bowls, no darker stems. In the tail of rule 11 b) ('Size is defined as number of character positions.') the full stop is an ordinary-weight period, indistinguishable from every other period on the page. The only bold glyphs anywhere on page 801 are the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' and the page-bottom license line, neither of which is at issue. So the claim's characterization of the PDF is accurate: there is no emphasis in this text.

Markdown side (specs/ISO_COBOL.md): the transcription does carry the emphasis markers, exactly as quoted. Lines 32468-32484 contain identifier-**4**, identifier-**1**, identifier-**7**, literal-**1**, identifier-**2**, identifier-**5** and identifier-**6**, plus 'character positions**.**' at the end of rule 11 b). The claim does not misquote either source.

That these markers are an artifact rather than a house convention is measurable: the bold-digit form occurs on just 9 lines in the whole 33k-line transcription, whereas the plain form 'identifier-N' occurs 1064 times. The convention throughout the document is plain text; page 801 is the deviation.

The tooling impact the claim asserts is real and I measured it rather than assuming it. `grep -c 'identifier-4'` over the whole spec returns 81 hits, but restricted to the UNSTRING general rule 11 region (lines 32460-32490) it returns 0 - despite rule 11 referencing identifier-4 four times. Any grep, anchor scan or citation tool keyed on the plain operand name silently skips the rule that defines the entire UNSTRING transfer algorithm. This is a retrieval defect, not merely an aesthetic one, though the normative text still renders correctly and no meaning is altered, so 'cosmetic' severity is defensible.

Two details in the claim's description are wrong and are corrected below: the artifact is not confined to this page, and it is not applied to every operand reference within rule 11.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with two corrections to the description.

Confirmed: markdown emphasis markers were injected around the trailing digit of operand names in UNSTRING general rule 11 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32468-32484), and around the terminating full stop of rule 11 b) ('character positions**.**'). PDF page 801 shows no bold in any of these positions - the body text is uniform roman, verified by 300 dpi glyph inspection of both named passages. Affected operands: identifier-**4**, identifier-**1**, identifier-**7**, literal-**1**, identifier-**2**, identifier-**5**, identifier-**6**.

Correction 1 - 'on this page only' is inaccurate. The same artifact appears on two further lines elsewhere in the transcription: line 14963 (ASSIGN clause implementor-defined rules - data-name-**1**, device-name-**1**, literal-**1**) and line 22824 (VALIDATE-STATUS general rule 8 - identifier-**2**). Page 801 accounts for 7 of the 9 affected lines, so it is the densest cluster but not the sole site. A repair sweep should cover all 9 lines, not just this page.

Correction 2 - the injection is not exhaustive within rule 11. The final operand reference in subrule g) ('until either all the characters are exhausted in the data item referenced by identifier-1') is left plain. That clause falls past the page-801 bottom margin and continues on PDF page 802, which is consistent with the corruption having been introduced by a per-page conversion step rather than by a global find-and-replace. Anyone repairing this must not assume a uniform pattern across the rule.

Impact, measured rather than asserted: `grep 'identifier-4'` returns 0 hits across lines 32460-32490 even though rule 11 references identifier-4 four times, so plain-name lookups miss the definition of the UNSTRING transfer algorithm entirely. Fix is a pure deletion of the '**' pairs; no wording changes.
